heroHeadline: ARTEMIS III HARDWARE OUTPACES ARTEMIS II SCHEDULE — ORION MODULES JOINED, ALL RS-25 ENGINES ON SITE; BLUE ORIGIN TRACES NEW GLENN EXPLOSION TO ENGINE VALVE, BLUE MOON MK1 SLIPS TO Q1 2027
heroSubtitle: Aug 10: Artemis III hardware assembly at Kennedy Space Center continues to outpace the equivalent point in the Artemis II campaign by roughly four months. The Orion crew and service modules were joined July 30 inside the Neil Armstrong Operations and Checkout Building, reusing more than 250 components from the Artemis II capsule that will carry astronauts Randy Bresnik, Andre Douglas, Frank Rubio, and ESA's Luca Parmitano; NASA said the combined spacecraft will next be powered on for the first time. All four RS-25 core-stage engines are now on site at the Vehicle Assembly Building following the final delivery July 21, with SLS solid rocket booster segments continuing to stack. On July 16, NASA selected SpaceX to fit Orion with two Starlink laser communications terminals for Artemis III, enabling 4K video downlink during the crew's Earth-orbit rendezvous and docking test with Starship and Blue Moon HLS test articles, targeting late 2027. MOON BASE: Four commercial lunar landers — Blue Origin, Firefly Aerospace, Intuitive Machines, and Voyager Technologies — cleared major testing milestones by August 4, with Voyager's Griffin-1 still targeting late-2026 delivery. SETBACK: Blue Origin said August 6 it traced the May 28 New Glenn static-fire explosion at LC-36 to a main oxygen valve issue on a BE-4 engine; modified hardware is due by end of August, but the debut flight of the Blue Moon Mark 1 cargo lander needed for Moon Base I's rover delivery has slipped from late summer 2026 to Q1 2027 at the earliest. NASA and Blue Origin agreed July 24 to conduct New Glenn second-stage hot fire testing at Stennis Space Center's B-2 stand starting this fall. SpaceX's Starship completed a fully successful IFT-13 flight July 24, splashing down intact after two earlier launch attempts were scrubbed. Artemis Accords now stand at 70 signatory nations after Serbia (69th, July 16) and Mauritius (70th, July 17) joined.
